title: Cache CFTC COT data in the DB and refresh it on a weekly schedule instead of fetching live on every request
description:
Follow-up from a backend-wide caching/scheduler audit this session, and an explicitly pre-approved follow-up to `backend-cftc-cot-data`'s own `decisions` entry: 'adding a caching layer (e.g. a new ORM table keyed by market+report_date, mirroring `IBKRBreadthSnapshotORM`) is a reasonable follow-up if this endpoint turns out to be called often enough that repeated CFTC round-trips matter, but was left out here as an unnecessary complication for a first, minimal version.' This task doesn't reverse that decision -- it exercises the follow-up it already named.

Confirmed via reading the current code before writing this task: `GET /api/cftc/cot` (`app/api/routers/cftc.py`) makes a live HTTP call to the CFTC's public Socrata endpoint via `CFTCCOTProvider.get_all_recent()` on *every single request*, with zero caching, TTL, or persistence of any kind -- `get_cftc_cot_provider` (`app/api/dependencies.py`) constructs a fresh, stateless instance per request with no shared cache state. The CFTC only publishes new Commitments of Traders data once a week (Fridays), so every request between weekly publications is fetching data that is, by definition, identical to the last fetch.

This is also the best-fit candidate for a scheduled (push-based) refresh rather than the lazy pull-based caching this app uses everywhere else (`CachedDataProvider`'s TTL-based OHLCV/extended-data caches): since the underlying data genuinely only changes on a known weekly cadence, a scheduled weekly pull is the *structurally correct* model here, not just a performance optimization layered on top of on-demand fetching. Confirmed this app already has a working, idiomatic pattern for exactly this kind of background job: `app/main.py`'s `lifespan()` already starts a long-running `asyncio.create_task(_ibkr_tickle_loop(provider))` background loop (45s interval, runs for the app's lifetime, logs-and-continues on failure) -- no new dependency (APScheduler/Celery) is needed; a second loop following that same shape is the lowest-friction path. No other cron/scheduler infrastructure exists anywhere in this repo (checked `.devcontainer/`, `scripts/`, `pyproject.toml`).

Out of scope for this task (a related but materially larger and more speculative idea surfaced by the same audit, deliberately not bundled in): pre-warming the OHLCV cache for watchlist/portfolio tickers ahead of market open via a similar scheduled job. That's a reasonable future follow-up (directly motivated by the real 2026-09-29 Yahoo 429 incident that originally prompted `backend-data-provider-timeouts`) but touches a much larger, already-TTL-cached data surface and deserves its own task if pursued -- don't expand this task's scope to cover it.

checklist.step: Design the DB cache table: a new `CFTCCOTCacheORM` (or similar name) keyed by market+report_date (mirroring `IBKRBreadthSnapshotORM`'s shape/conventions), storing whatever fields `COTWeeklyReport` currently exposes. Add the Alembic migration. Decide and record (decisions entry) whether to key by `COT_MARKETS`' market_key or the raw CFTC contract code, and how many weeks of history to persist (matching `CFTCCOTProvider.WEEKS_OF_HISTORY` or independently decided).

Wire `GET /api/cftc/cot` to read from the new cache table first, falling back to a live CFTC fetch only on a genuine cache miss (e.g. first-ever startup before the scheduled job has run once) -- mirroring `CachedDataProvider`'s existing read-through pattern and its already-established `IntegrityError`/`OperationalError`-catch convention for concurrent-write races on the cache table.

Add a second `asyncio.create_task`-based background loop in `app/main.py`'s `lifespan()`, following `_ibkr_tickle_loop`'s existing shape/error-handling conventions, that refreshes the CFTC cache on a weekly cadence (research and decide the exact trigger -- e.g. a fixed day/time check each loop iteration vs. a simple "refresh if the cached data is more than N days old" check -- and record as a decisions entry). Must log-and-continue on failure, matching the existing loop's resilience behavior, never crash the app.

Update `GET /api/cftc/cot`'s docstring and the `backend-cftc-cot-data` task's own description are NOT to be edited retroactively (append-only decisions convention) -- instead record this task's own decisions entry referencing and fulfilling the original task's pre-approved follow-up, per CLAUDE.md's decision-memory convention.

Tests (no live network calls per Testing.md): the cache read-through logic (hit/miss/stale paths), the scheduled refresh loop's trigger logic (mocked clock/time, not a real 1-week wait), and a concurrent-write race test for the new cache table mirroring the existing `CachedDataProvider` upsert-race tests' pattern. Regenerate `backend/openapi.json` if `GET /api/cftc/cot`'s documented behavior/response shape changes in any way.

decisions.decision: `CFTCCOTCacheORM` (app/db/models.py) is keyed by `(market_key, report_date)` -- this app's own stable `app.data.cftc_cot_provider.COT_MARKETS` label (`"eur"`/`"jpy"`/`"oil"`/`"gold"`/`"bonds"`) -- not the CFTC's raw `cftc_contract_market_code`. Persists up to `CFTCCOTProvider.WEEKS_OF_HISTORY` (52) rows per market, matching the provider's own fetch window rather than an independently chosen length; unlike `OHLCVCacheORM`/`ExtendedDataCacheORM` (left to grow forever, since full history is directly useful to those), `CFTCCOTCache.refresh` actively deletes any existing row for a market that falls outside a fresh `get_all_recent()` response's own window on every refresh, since this app's own `cot_index` computation never looks past its own trailing `weeks_of_history` window -- an older row serves no purpose once it ages out, so leaving it behind would just accumulate unboundedly over months/years with no corresponding benefit.
decisions.rationale: `market_key` was chosen over the raw CFTC contract code because it's this app's own stable, user-facing identifier (the same one `CFTCMarketKey`'s API-schema Literal and every other part of this feature already key by) -- a cache keyed by the provider's own data-shape-specific code would couple this table's primary key to a CFTC-internal identifier this app otherwise treats as an implementation detail (see `backend-cftc-cot-data`'s own decisions entry: CFTC has already renamed two of the five underlying contracts' *display names* once without the app needing to change anything, precisely because `market_key` -- not the raw code or name -- is what's actually persisted/exposed). The trade-off accepted: if `COT_MARKETS`' key-to-contract-code mapping itself were ever remapped (not just renamed), a cache keyed by `market_key` wouldn't detect that as a logical change and would keep serving the old contract's now-stale-by-identity data until the next scheduled refresh overwrites it -- judged an acceptable risk since that mapping is a rare, deliberate code change (not a runtime event), not something this app needs to defend against automatically. 52 weeks/pruning was chosen over leaving the table to grow forever (OHLCVCacheORM's own precedent) because this table's read path (`CFTCCOTCache.get_cached_reports`) only ever needs enough history to match `get_all_recent()`'s own bounded response -- unlike OHLCV, where arbitrarily long history is a real, independent use case (indicator warm-up, long lookback windows) -- so unbounded retention here would be pure waste with no offsetting benefit.

decisions.decision: The scheduled refresh (`app.main._cftc_cot_refresh_loop`) wakes every `_CFTC_COT_REFRESH_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (6 hours) and refreshes only if `CFTCCOTCache.is_stale(_CFTC_COT_CACHE_MAX_AGE)` -- the cache is empty, or its newest fetch is >= 6 days old -- rather than anchoring to CFTC's actual Friday release schedule (e.g. "refresh every Friday at HH:MM ET").
decisions.rationale: CFTC doesn't publish an exact time-of-day for its weekly release (only "Friday", per `backend-cftc-cot-data`'s own research), and that release can also slip around a CFTC-observed holiday -- a fixed day/time trigger would need its own holiday-calendar logic this app has no other use for, just to avoid either missing a delayed release or firing on a day nothing new was actually published. A periodic "is my cached snapshot older than N days" check is simpler (no calendar logic at all), self-correcting (a missed or delayed check doesn't permanently fall behind -- the very next 6-hourly check still catches it), and needs no new dependency (APScheduler/croniter), matching `_ibkr_tickle_loop`'s existing `asyncio.create_task` background-loop shape exactly. 6 hours for the check interval and 6 days (not a full 7) for the staleness threshold were chosen together deliberately: 6 days gives the 6-hour check cadence a full day of slack before a 7-day-exact threshold would otherwise flap in and out of "stale" depending on which exact 6-hour tick a request happened to land on relative to the prior week's refresh time, while still refreshing (at the latest) within one day of a new Friday release in every case. Alternatives considered: a fixed Friday-afternoon-ET trigger was rejected for the holiday-calendar/exact-time reasons above; a much shorter check interval (e.g. matching `_IBKR_TICKLE_INTERVAL_SECONDS`'s 45s) was rejected as pointless churn -- `is_stale`'s own DB query is cheap, but there's no reason to run it thousands of times between any two weekly releases when 6 hours is already far more granular than the data's own weekly cadence requires.

decisions.decision: `GET /api/cftc/cot` reads from `CFTCCOTCache` first; on a genuine cache miss (at least one of the 5 fixed markets has no cached row at all -- e.g. before the scheduled loop's first run since this app started, or a partially-completed earlier refresh), it falls back to a live `CFTCCOTProvider.get_all_recent()` call and populates the cache with that result before responding. Once every market has at least one cached row, this endpoint never re-checks staleness or re-fetches live on its own -- that's solely the scheduled background loop's job.
decisions.rationale: This fulfills checklist item 2 literally ("falling back to a live CFTC fetch only on a genuine cache miss") and keeps the endpoint always answerable (no window where it 500s/503s purely because the scheduled loop hasn't run yet) without reintroducing the per-request live-fetch cost this whole task exists to remove. Deliberately NOT layering a TTL-style staleness re-check on top of this read path (unlike every other cache in this codebase, `CachedDataProvider`/`IndicatorHistoryResponseCache`) -- see this task's description for why a scheduled push is structurally correct here (the CFTC only republishes weekly, a known fact, not a per-call guess), so adding a second staleness check at the read layer would just be redundant work against the same underlying fact the scheduled loop already handles, while also undermining the whole point of caching if a transient slow 6-hour window after the loop's own check fell right before an on-demand request (a TTL re-check at read time would currently always find it 'still valid' anyway, since 6 days wide margin from the loop's own cadence, so this is not a live divergence case, just an unnecessary extra check path to maintain).

decisions.decision: This task fulfills -- rather than reverses -- `backend-cftc-cot-data`'s own `decisions` entry (docs/tasks/done/backend-cftc-cot-data.json), which explicitly named this exact follow-up as reasonable once the endpoint turns out to be called often enough that repeated CFTC round-trips matter: "adding a caching layer (e.g. a new ORM table keyed by market+report_date, mirroring `IBKRBreadthSnapshotORM`) is a reasonable follow-up... but was left out here as an unnecessary complication for a first, minimal version." `backend-cftc-cot-data.json` itself is left untouched (append-only decisions convention, per CLAUDE.md) -- this entry is the record of that follow-up being exercised.
decisions.rationale: Per CLAUDE.md's decision-memory convention, a correction or follow-up to a prior decision is recorded as a new entry on the task doing the follow-up work, not by editing the original task's already-`done` file -- this entry (and this task generally) is exactly that.

decisions.decision: Needs-work rework for PR #380's review: updated `docs/architecture/Backend.md` §9 (and §2's module-layout tree, §7's cache-table prose) and `docs/architecture/API.md`'s `GET /api/cftc/cot` section to describe the actual, now-shipped caching/scheduling behavior (DB-backed `CFTCCOTCache` read-through, `_cftc_cot_refresh_loop` scheduled background refresh), replacing the stale "fetches fresh on every request, no local caching in this minimal scope" claims both docs still had. Also folded in both non-blocking findings already filed on `backend-cftc-cot-caching-scheduler-followups` while making this same pass, since both were small and low-risk: (1) Backend.md §2/§7 already needed touching for the blocking fix itself, so adding the `cftc_cot_cache.py`/table mentions there cost nothing extra; (2) added `TestLifespanCftcCotRefreshLoop.test_shutdown_does_not_block_on_an_in_flight_refresh_call` (backend/tests/unit/test_main.py), mirroring `TestLifespanIbkrTickleGate`'s identical test for the IBKR loop's same `asyncio.to_thread`+`Future.cancel()` pattern -- confirmed effective by temporarily removing the `cftc_cot_refresh_task.cancel()` call and observing the test hang/fail before reverting that mutation.
decisions.rationale: The doc staleness fix was blocking (pr-reviewer's own verdict) and is addressed directly rather than deferred. Both non-blocking items were judged low-risk to fold in now rather than leave on the followups task: the doc-tree/table-prose item is a few extra lines added to a file this PR was already editing for the blocking fix, and the shutdown test is a small, well-contained addition that mirrors an existing, already-reviewed pattern verbatim (same loop shape, same cancellation mechanism, same test structure) rather than new design work. Marked both items `done` on `backend-cftc-cot-caching-scheduler-followups.json` in the same commit rather than leaving them open there now that they're actually fixed, per the task-board's own 'don't let the board drift from reality' expectation -- that followups task's own `depends_on: [backend-cftc-cot-caching-scheduler]` and its two checklist items are otherwise now stale once this lands.

decisions.decision: Also fixed a third, later-added blocking review comment on PR #380 (posted as a follow-up PR comment after the review object already in this task's `review` field was written, but recorded there as blocking in `review.comments[2]`/`review.notes`): `_cftc_cot_refresh_loop` previously slept the full `_CFTC_COT_REFRESH_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (6h) before its very first staleness check, copied verbatim from `_ibkr_tickle_loop`'s sleep-first shape. Restructured so the loop now calls a new `_check_and_refresh_cftc_cot_cache_once` helper once immediately on startup, before entering the sleep-then-check loop, so a cache already stale at app restart (any downtime >= `_CFTC_COT_CACHE_MAX_AGE`) is corrected right away rather than being served as a stale cache hit for up to a further 6 hours. Added a dedicated regression test (`test_refreshes_immediately_on_startup_without_waiting_for_the_first_sleep`) with a deliberately long check interval to prove the refresh fires before the first sleep, not only after it -- mutation-tested by temporarily reverting to the old sleep-first order and confirming the new test fails (times out) against it. Also had to add/adjust test infrastructure (`_stub_cftc_refresh_check` module-level autouse fixture + its override inside `TestLifespanCftcCotRefreshLoop`, and a provider mock added to `test_cancelled_cleanly_on_shutdown`) since the immediate-on-startup check meant every other test in `tests/unit/test_main.py` that calls `lifespan()` would otherwise now construct a real `CFTCCOTProvider` and attempt a live network call/real on-disk DB touch the instant the app's lifespan starts, violating Testing.md's no-live-network-calls rule.
decisions.rationale: Per this agent's own instruction to treat every entry in a needs_work review's `comments` as a required fix rather than optional feedback, not just the findings explicitly summarized when this rework was dispatched -- this comment was present in the task JSON's `review.comments` (with `review.notes` explicitly calling it a second blocking item) even though it arrived via a later PR comment rather than the original review post. Fixed it in this same PR rather than leaving it for a follow-up, consistent with how the two originally-named blocking doc findings were handled, since leaving a real correctness gap in this loop (its own docstring/decisions entry already state it's the cache's sole freshness guarantee) unaddressed would defeat that guarantee for any real restart scenario.

comments.summary: [round 1, fixed] docs/architecture/Backend.md §9 and docs/architecture/API.md's GET /api/cftc/cot section both still affirmatively state there is no local caching/persistence layer and that the endpoint fetches fresh on every request -- this PR's entire point is to add exactly that caching layer and reverse that "minimal scope" framing, but neither doc was touched. Fixed in the round-2 push: both docs (plus Backend.md §2/§7) now accurately and thoroughly describe the DB-backed CFTCCOTCache read-through + _cftc_cot_refresh_loop scheduled background refresh -- verified by reading both docs in full in round 2, no stale language remains.

[round 1, fixed] docs/architecture/API.md's GET /api/cftc/cot section has the same stale "fetched fresh on every request -- no local caching in this minimal scope" claim as Backend.md §9. Fixed alongside the Backend.md fix above; verified in round 2.

[round 1 follow-up comment, fixed] _cftc_cot_refresh_loop sleeps for the full 6-hour check interval before its very first staleness check (copied from _ibkr_tickle_loop's sleep-first shape, which is harmless there since an IBKR session is inherently fresh at connect time -- but the CFTC cache is persisted on-disk state whose staleness depends on calendar time since the last refresh, not this process's uptime). Since GET /api/cftc/cot's read path deliberately never re-checks staleness itself (decisions entry: the scheduled loop is the sole freshness guarantee), a cache already past _CFTC_COT_CACHE_MAX_AGE (6 days) when the app restarts after any >=6-day downtime gets no correction for a further 6 hours after startup, during which stale data is served as a cache hit. Fixed: the loop now calls a new _check_and_refresh_cftc_cot_cache_once helper immediately on startup before the first asyncio.sleep. Confirmed genuinely existed (not fabricated) via `gh pr view 380 --json comments`, and confirmed the fix via mutation testing in round 2: reverting to the old sleep-first order makes the new regression test (test_refreshes_immediately_on_startup_without_waiting_for_the_first_sleep) fail/time out; restored afterward, file diff against HEAD was empty.

review.notes: Round 2 re-review of task-worker's rework. All three round-1 blocking findings (see comments above) independently re-verified as genuinely fixed, not just claimed -- read both updated architecture docs in full, read the final app/main.py / cftc_cot_cache.py / routers/cftc.py / db/models.py / tests in full (not just the diff) given task-worker's self-reported mid-session accidental `git checkout -- backend/app/main.py`, and found no duplicate/orphaned code or conflict markers. Mutation-tested both the startup-immediate-refresh fix (reverted to sleep-first -> new test fails/times out; restored, clean diff) and the shutdown-doesn't-block-on-an-in-flight-refresh test (removed the `.cancel()` call, kept the `await` -> test hangs/times out as expected; restored, clean diff). Checked the new autouse `_stub_cftc_refresh_check` fixture didn't weaken any `TestLifespanIbkrTickleGate` test -- each still asserts genuine IBKR-loop behavior; the `create_task_spy.call_count`/`spy_return_list[0]` adjustments are legitimate accounting for the new always-on CFTC task, not a weakening. Independently verified: pytest --cov=app --cov-fail-under=90 (1569 passed, 100% coverage, matches claim), ruff/mypy clean, openapi.json re-regenerated and byte-identical to the committed snapshot (docstring-only description change, matches the diff), migration f9c52e69b04a round-tripped cleanly (upgrade/downgrade/upgrade) against a scratch SQLite DB. backend-cftc-cot-caching-scheduler-followups.json's two checklist items are both marked done and the claimed test/doc additions are genuinely present. scripts/validate_tasks.py reports the board structurally clean. No frontend changes in this PR (0 lines under frontend/) -- browser walkthrough and e2e suite steps correctly not applicable, stated explicitly. No new blocking or non-blocking findings from this round.
